_purpose: Numbers the documentation publishes as measured evidence, in one place, so a claim and the thing it claims cannot drift apart silently. Each claim lists where docs cite it and what measures it; two mechanical checks close the loop. tools/check_docs.mjs fails if a cited_in file stops containing the value's prefix (a doc that quietly drops or rewrites an evidence number is caught). CI's roots-in-a-browser job fails if the boot's actual output hash differs from the value here (a boot that changes its printed line without updating the claim is caught). A green run therefore means the published number IS the measured number, not that someone remembered.

suite_size.what: The workspace's measured test total, as `cargo test -q` reports it summed across the per-suite lines. It is on the README's front page, which is the place most likely to be read and the place that drifted furthest once - a status board saying '32 tests' while the suite held 183 is a public lie, not a stale number.
suite_size.measured_by: `cargo test -q` - the sum of the `test result: ok.` lines

device_arm_skips_on_demo_scene.what: How many union second children the device's own bound-skip arm refused to evaluate while marching the demo scene's 3,072 rays, tallied per ray inside the shader by `march_rays_counted` and summed on the host. The published form carries a thousands separator; the CI line prints the bare integer (`the device refused 22237 union second children, on 2640 of 3072 rays`), so this claim is the docs' spelling of a measured number, not a separately-derived one.
device_arm_skips_on_demo_scene.measured_by: the `Demo scene from content on a device` step's `arm measured` line on the ARM64 macOS runner (Apple Paravirtual device); it is an informational row, and nothing hashes it

cpu_bound_layer_avoided_on_demo_scene.what: The CPU cull layer's node entries avoided over the same 3,072 rays and the same tree, measured by counting `visit`s with the table against counting them with every skip refused. It is the upper bound the device figure above is a subset of, so the two claims move together or not at all: the arm on the device asks only plain unions and leaves its bound unclamped, while this layer also takes smooth unions (OQ-54) and clamps.
cpu_bound_layer_avoided_on_demo_scene.measured_by: the `Demo scene from content on a device` step's `arm pricing` line on all three architectures, and `crates/render/tests/cull.rs`'s enclosure tests for the bound arithmetic underneath it

boot_output_sha256.what: SHA-256 of the whole eighteen-line output of `cargo run -p engine` (seventeen before the peer-reconcile line arrived, sixteen before the stream-carry line), which is the artifact the determinism claim is about: native, the bare-V8 shim run, Chromium on three architectures and Safari/JavaScriptCore all produce these bytes.
boot_output_sha256.measured_by: the `roots in a browser` job's `native sha256` line, and `roots in JavaScriptCore (Safari)`'s `safari sha256` line

superseded.why: repointing a citation that wrongly named OQ-46 (wire identities) as the owner of divergence resolution also edited a word inside the boot's own printed peer-reconcile line, so the whole-output bytes moved again while every hashed vector stayed put. Caught by CI's browser leg comparing the run against this manifest - the local gate cannot see it, because the root lines are unchanged and the citing files still agreed with the stale value: a claim checked only against other claims is not checked at all

A printed line grew, so the whole-output bytes moved; no hashed value did: EPOCH_0, REGIONS, SLOT_TABLE and REGION_0 still agree with doc 03, and the WASM leg still matches native line for line

A printed line grew, so the whole-output bytes moved; no hashed value did - EPOCH_0, REGIONS, SLOT_TABLE and the re-entered REGION_0 still agree with doc 03, and the WASM leg still matches native line for line

the region line now also prints what the descent charges - 174,881 evaluations against 57,665 with each region's own children asked, and 1,039 rays proved empty against 2,260. The whole-output bytes move; no hashed value does: EPOCH_0, REGIONS, SLOT_TABLE and the re-entered REGION_0 still agree with doc 03, and the WASM leg still matches the native build line for line

The demo's scene blends at its root, so the descent is refused there and both culled paths report the same 179072 evaluations and 666 of 3072 rays - the added clause is a measured refusal, not a new number. boot_output_sha256._note_value_change: measured by 38327470938 (all ten definitions green: the sixteen-line output, terrain-scale region cells included, is identical in native, bare V8, Chromium x3 architectures and Safari/JavaScriptCore)

ray_descent_refused_on_r1_grid.what: Rays the licensed per-ray descent proves cannot reach the boot scene, over R1's own 1920x1080 grid (2,073,600 rays) with the boot's own camera, `max_t` 40 and surface 1e-3 - 41.1% of the grid and 48.1% of the 1,770,173 rays the GTX 1070 measured as finding no surface. The root bound alone refuses 0 of the same grid, which is why this number and not the scene sphere is the price of the arm.
ray_descent_refused_on_r1_grid.measured_by: the `R1's ray-level cull priced before the arm` step, whose own lines reproduce 0 / 851,956 / 12,698,979 / 1,104 identically on x86-64 Windows, ARM64 macOS and x86-64 Linux, plus `crates/render/tests/cull.rs` for the enclosure arithmetic underneath it

cached_frame_stale_after_camera_pan.what: Depth pixels the temporal cache's own frame disagreed with an uncacheable full march after the camera panned and EVERY pixel was invalidated - out of 230,400, on a 640x360 grid, in the first moved frame. The number that turned the cache's published dynamic rows from measurements into a claim about a picture that cannot show motion: a dirty pixel can be repaired by re-marching, but here it was repaired by re-reading a cached surface that had nothing to do with the new camera.
cached_frame_stale_after_camera_pan.measured_by: `crates/gpu/examples/r1_cached_dynamic_loop.rs`, camera-policy frame 1, run on this machine's GeForce MX250 at 640x360. It is NOT a CI step: the example exits 1 by design until the second cache layer is fixed (task #120), and a step whose expected colour is red is a note, not a gate. No duration from it is admissible for R1 - that needs the GTX 1070.

cached_frame_stale_after_entity_slide.what: The worst repaired-disagreement the entity policy reaches after six frames of the sphere sliding and the union of its old and new footprints being invalidated - 21,424 of the 151,751 pixels the dirty mask actually marked, with 28,190 stale before the invalidation. The old footprint is invalidated as well as the new one on purpose: a pixel the entity vacated shows whatever stands behind it, so leaving it clean is a stale pixel by definition.
cached_frame_stale_after_entity_slide.measured_by: `crates/gpu/examples/r1_cached_dynamic_loop.rs`, entity-policy frame 6, run on this machine's GeForce MX250 at 640x360. Same disclaimer as the row above: not a CI step, exits 1 until task #120 lands, and carries no admissible R1 duration.

gate_p1_5_targets.what_it_is: Ubuntu 24.04 server, AMD Ryzen 5 5500 (AVX2+FMA), glibc, its own LLVM 21 toolchain - a fourth execution environment no CI image or workstation represents
The other real machine: Windows x86-64 with an RTX 3050 6GB, i.e. an Ampere GPU on a driver stack that can present one (the 1070 box is on nouveau, so no nvidia-smi and no usable Vulkan)

_gate_p1_5_targets_purpose: Gate P1.5's demo clause named four machines the project's owner does not have - an AVX2-less N2600, an RTX 3060 desktop, a Linux-Mesa box and an M1 browser - so it looked like a test awaiting a result while being unclosable in principle. Amended 2026-10-13 to the two devices that exist. The axes neither can express are named rather than dropped: the no-AVX2 Celeron axis is carried by CI's blake3/pure scalar-vector leg and tools/cpu_codegen_parity.sh (baseline versus -Ctarget-cpu=x86-64-v3), and Apple-silicon JavaScriptCore by the roots-in-JavaScriptCore job on the ARM64 runner. Those are proxies for a compiler and an engine, not for silicon. A device row may read agrees only with a resolvable commit, the current whole-output digest and the legs that actually ran.
